Done. I've set up the sync to run automatically when your machine boots:

**What was configured:**
1. **Created `run-sync.ps1`** — A PowerShell wrapper that runs the sync.sh script with the proper environment
2. **Created a Startup shortcut** — Placed in your Startup folder so it launches automatically on boot
   - Runs hidden (no visible window)
   - Set to launch with elevated permissions
   - Will run the sync script from the correct directory

**How it works:**
- On next boot, Windows will automatically execute the sync script
- The sync logs timestamps to `data/feed.log`
- No user intervention needed—it just runs

To verify it's working, you can manually trigger it by opening the Startup folder and double-clicking the shortcut, or restart your machine to test the automatic launch.
